records.ground: `exec` streams the invoked command's own stdout and stderr and emits no result document of its own — it carries no output-format flag — so there is no structured rendering for a case to choose between.

These operations neither create nor attach to a container: they resolve configuration, build an image, resolve Feature versions, scaffold files, or probe the host. A pre-existing container is therefore not a condition they can observe or act on, and only the degenerate `none` state remains meaningful.

`exec` attaches to a container another operation created; it never resolves, orders, or installs Features. Whether the target container has Features at all is visible to it, but the ordering and lockfile-resolution decisions belong to `up`/`build`, and a case pinning those decisions is a case for that operation.

`down` removes resources identified by labels and the Compose project name, `doctor` reports host and runtime diagnostics, and `templates apply` scaffolds files into a workspace. None of the three resolves or installs a Feature, so Feature composition cannot change what they do or what they emit.

An image-metadata layer is read from the `devcontainer.metadata` label of a resolved image. These operations never resolve or inspect an image — they remove labelled resources, query a Feature registry, rewrite a lockfile, scaffold files, or probe the host — so no image-derived layer can exist to contribute to their effective configuration.

`doctor` reports host, runtime, and environment diagnostics rather than a merged configuration; it never resolves an extends chain or applies a command-line overlay, so how a configuration would have been layered cannot affect the diagnosis it prints.

`down` and `run-user-commands` complete with progress and diagnostics only; neither carries an output-format flag and neither writes a result document to stdout, so a structured rendering does not exist for a case to observe.

`read-configuration` and `up` emit their result exclusively as a single JSON document on stdout; neither carries an output-format flag, so a human-readable rendering of the result does not exist and cannot be exercised.
